commonsFile: View inside the TRIGA research reactor at the Jožef Stefan Institute.jpg
author: Sbaletsk
why: Looking down into the pool of a TRIGA research reactor, cooling tubes and instrument holders over glowing blue-green water: the experimental nuclear physics hardware the degree trains on (CTU also runs a training reactor).
cropNote: Top-down view of rods, pipes and the reactor pool in turquoise; a tiny round sticker top right is unreadable at 480 px, no text legible.

commonsFile: CSIRO ScienceImage 2459 Prototype computerised geological core logger.jpg
author: North Sullivan Photography, CSIRO
why: Two geologists in hard hats logging drill core laid out in trays with an automated core-scanning rig: the core logging that engineering geology, exploration drilling and geophysics degrees train for.
cropNote: Kept both geologists, the rows of core on the roller tray and the scanner gantry; the monitor text is an illegible green-on-black blur at 480 px; no logos or signs readable.

commonsFile: In-stream inoculation addition while molten cast iron is poured to a green sand mold in a foundry in Bangladesh.jpg
author: Sm faysal
why: Molten iron streaming into a sand mould at a foundry: how metals are cast and processed, the production side of a materials engineering degree.
cropNote: Dark crop dominated by the glowing orange pour and sparks with the mould line lit beside it; no people, no text. Darkish by nature (firelight), the glow carries it.

commonsFile: Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests - Timber Sales - Tree Measuring and Marking (20181206-FS-APACHE-SITGREAVES-LSC-0729).jpg
author: USDAgov
why: A forestry crew talking through a stand in a snowy pine forest with a tablet and marked stump: the field work of forest management and natural resource planning.
cropNote: Four foresters in hard hats and hi-vis vests among pine trunks and a stump; the tablet screen is not legible and there is no signage, logo text or number readable at 480 px.

author: Dan Kollmann
why: A combine harvester cutting ripe wheat in a dust haze: the agricultural machinery this engineering degree is about.
cropNote: Green combine head-on at the edge of a wheat field with dust behind; the small maker badge is not legible at 480 px, no other text, no people.

author: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
why: A chemist in protective glasses and a leather glove glassblowing a laboratory reaction vessel over a flame: the glassware craft of chemical technology, in a country famed for glass.
cropNote: Crop keeps her face in tinted goggles, the glowing glass flask in a clamp and the bench clutter at left; no legible text or logos.

author: CSAR ACE
why: Zebrafish swimming in a blue research tank: the model organism used for genetics and developmental biology in life-science labs.
cropNote: Crop is the whole tank of striped zebrafish against blue water; no people, no text, no labels legible.

commonsFile: Nieten einer im Abbau befindlichen Stahlbrücke.jpg
author: August Geyler
why: Close view of the riveted steel girder of an old bridge being cut apart with a torch: structural steel, the connections and members a structural engineer learns to design and assess.
cropNote: Crop keeps the row of round rivet heads down a dark steel flange with the orange flame and a tiny figure out of focus at the far end; no text or numbers readable.

commonsFile: Timber frame house under construction, New Zealand.jpg
author: L Maule
why: A timber-framed house under construction, studs, rafters and floor joists standing before any walls: building construction at its structural stage, the specialisation of this degree.
cropNote: Crop keeps the whole open frame against blue sky with stacked timber at the base; no people, signs or text.

commonsFile: Ford Bowers printing photographs in Dow Photographic Laboratory - DPLA - e3bd18f48093cf13c394dda1fd42c2b6.jpg
author: Dow Chemical Company
why: A photographer in a brick-walled darkroom working at an enlarger and print easel, handling a sheet of paper: darkroom printing, the craft base of photography studies.
cropNote: Black-and-white crop of the man bent over the easel beside a tall enlarger column, paper trays and shelves; no legible text, labels or numbers.

author: Till Niermann
why: Looking down the line of hydraulic roof supports of a longwall coal face, the mechanised underground mining system, preserved in a German mining museum's demonstration mine: the equipment underground coal mining engineers plan and operate.
cropNote: Crop runs down the tunnel of white steel chocks and yellow shearer at left in museum lighting; no people; small stencils on the supports are not legible at 480 px. A museum demonstration mine, not a working face.
